newsitem.title: UK: London platinum prices soar, break through $400.
newsitem.headline: London platinum prices soar, break through $400.

text.p: Prices of the rare white metal platinum shot to over $406 per ounce on Friday for the first time since May last year before speculators took their profits out of an overheating market.
Dealers said concerns over the non-appearance of Russian exports of the precious metal so far this year were fuelling demand especially in Japan, the largest consumer of platinum.
It was fixed at $398.75 its highest since August 29 1996 and helped pull gold to its highest fix since January 3 of $360.60.
Platinum's sister metal palladium fixed at $155.00, $2.00 below Thursday's highest fixing since July 11, 1995.
Russia is the leading producer of palladium and the second largest exporter of platinum after South Africa.
"There is still no sign of Russia opening trade talks with Japan. It all depends on them now," one dealer said.
"$400 is a very significant psychological price," he added.
Changes to Russia's exporting administration and delays in passing the 1997 budget postponed the start of negotiations with Japanese importers and consequently exports.
Compounding the situation was a statement on February 26 from a union official that Russia's Norilsk mining and metallurgical complex would be struck on March 15.
Workers at the cash-strapped plant in Arctic Siberia have not been paid since last October.
"There are a lot of problems in Russia and although people will take profits out, the market will continue to firm until Russia and Japan sit down to talk," the dealer said.
According to technical analysts who examine charts of historical prices to determine future moves, there could be hiccups along the way.
"Platinum's rise has been vertical and that cannot be sustained," said Elli Gifford, technical analyst at Investment Research of Cambridge.
She noted that all the technical target prices had been fulfilled so far and the next thing would be a challenge of the Spring 1996 high of $407.00.
"I can't talk it up much higher than that," she said.
Cliff Green a chartist at Trend Analysis was equally emphatic. "Once this phase is over it will fall rapidly," he said, adding that very volatile prices were likely next week.
Platinum is used in jewellery, electronics, many chemical industry applications and in autocatalysts to remove toxic gases from car exhaust fumes.
Palladium is also used in catalytic converters, electronics and chemicals and as major constituent in dental alloys.
Annual production of both metals is small compared with gold and essentially limited to Russia and South Africa.
According to leading refiner Johnson Matthey platinum production totalled 4.98 million ounces in 1995 of which 3.37 million ounces were from South Africa and 1.28 million ounces exported from Russia.
Palladium availability totalled 6.34 million ounces of which 4.20 million came from Russia, about half of which was from the government stockpile, and 1.6 million from South Africa.
Reflecting the impact of losing its Russian supplies, Japan imports of platinum and palladium from the dealer market surged in January, according to Finance Ministry statistics issued on Friday.
Palladium imports jumped 224 percent compared with January 1995 to 8.15 tonnes and platinum purchases were up 63.6 percent to 7.1 tonnes compared with the previous year.

"Because we expected Japan-Russia platinum group metal export talks to be delayed we have stepped up our spot market buying since the end of last year," an official at a major Japanese bullion house said.
